title: The general thanksgiving (1662)
hook: for our creation, preservation, and all the blessings of this life
carry: all the blessings of this life
tomorrow: what kind of peace can't anyone hand you?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: spare thou them. The confession put the undone things first. Today the same prayer book says thank you.

Kitchen table, the morning after a birthday. A stack of blank cards, a pen, and a parent's rule: one card per gift, and name the gift. Thank you for the sweater. Thank you for the book. One note, one thing. The 1662 Book of Common Prayer has a thank-you note that breaks the rule. It names three things at once, each one enormous, and then adds a fourth with the words above all.
screen: `ONE CARD, ONE GIFT.` → `A NOTE THAT BREAKS THE RULE.` → `THREE THINGS, THEN ABOVE ALL.`

segments.voice: It's called the general thanksgiving, and it opens: "Almighty God, Father of all mercies." Then the heart of it: "We bless thee for our creation, preservation, and all the blessings of this life." Take them one at a time. Creation: that you exist at all, that there's a you to say thanks. Preservation: that you've been kept going, through nights and illnesses and hard years; a cousin of Luther's morning thanks a few days back. And all the blessings of this life: bread, friends, a good chair, a song you love. Then the prayer lifts its eyes: "but above all for thine inestimable love in the redemption of the world by our Lord Jesus Christ; for the means of grace, and for the hope of glory." Ordinary gifts first, then the one Christians count above all. Then it asks for one thing: that hearts may be truly thankful, and that God's praise be shown "not only with our lips, but in our lives." The detail worth passing on: the note doesn't end with the thanks. It ends asking that the thanks move out of the mouth and into how the day is lived.
screen: `CREATION.` · `PRESERVATION.` · `ALL THE BLESSINGS OF THIS LIFE.` · `NOT ONLY WITH OUR LIPS.` · then, large: `ABOVE ALL.`

segments.voice: If there's paper near, write three short lines by hand: creation, preservation, blessings. Next to each, add one plain example from your own life: that you're here, one way you've been kept going, one good thing from this week. If you pray, you can give thanks for each line as you write it.
The general thanksgiving. The prayer book's thanks for creation, preservation and every blessing of this life, and above all for God's love in Christ.
Keep this line: all the blessings of this life, the ordinary ones included. That's day sixteen forty-six.

screen: `DAY 1646 COUNTS.` → `THE SAINTS IN THEIR OWN WORDS · 45 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT KIND OF PEACE CAN'T ANYONE HAND YOU?`

fork.setup: after a long week, your friend says she has nothing to be thankful for: no win, no good news. what would the general thanksgiving point to first?
options: that she's here at all, and has been kept going.
waiting until something good actually happens.
listing her friends' wins instead of her own.
fork.reveal: the prayer starts with creation and preservation, being here and being kept, then all the blessings of this life.

chat.says: nia's great-grandma had a good day! stories, pie, knew everyone. nia says 'i'm thankful but to who?'
options: Tell her who you'd thank, God, and why. Then name the gifts with her: stories, pie, a good day.
Tell her thanks doesn't count unless it's said to God, so she should start praying.
Tell her thanks is for big things; save it for if her great-grandma gets better.
